title: Input, Process, Output
goals: Trace information through a system without confusing information with a physical action
Explain which details a representation preserves or discards
Locate the earliest stage at which an incorrect result could have arisen
vocabulary: A way of recording information so that it can be stored, communicated or processed
Information supplied to a particular process
An operation that changes, selects or interprets information
The result produced by a process
Details that cannot be recovered from the retained representation

blocks.text: Consider two catalogue records. Book A has 90 pages and is about a child solving a seaside mystery. Book B has 90 pages and is about a lost spaceship. If we keep only page count, both become the number 90. The number is useful for a length limit, but it cannot tell us which story is a mystery. Information that was never retained cannot be recovered just by calculating harder.

rows: Does it match a mystery request?
Will this particular reader enjoy it?
What does the description say happens?
What exact sentence occurs on page 42?

blocks.text: The phrase cannot settle alone matters. A genre tag might be inaccurate, and a reader might enjoy an unfamiliar genre. A representation is useful only in relation to a question and its limits. More detail is not automatically better: unnecessary personal information can add risk without helping the task.

guided_practice.title: Finish the visitor example
guided_practice.prompt: A record stores only total visitors=3. Give two different arrival schedules that produce this total. Can the total tell us the busiest hour? Explain.
guided_practice.answer: Examples: three visitors at 09:00, or one each at 09:00, 10:00 and 11:00. Both total 3, but their busiest-hour patterns differ. The total lacks arrival-time information, so the busiest hour cannot be recovered from it alone.

independent_case.title: Investigate a new loss of information
independent_case.task: A classroom device receives four scores and stores only their total, 20. A student claims that every score must be 5. Give two different lists of four nonnegative whole-number scores with total 20. Explain precisely what the stored total establishes and what it does not.
independent_case.answer: For example [5,5,5,5] and [2,4,6,8] both total 20. The stored total establishes the sum under the stated recording process, but not the individual scores or their equality. A list with fewer than four entries or a different total is not a valid counterexample.
independent_case.source: primary source W4, first curriculum occurrence

misconceptions: Every output is the final action
Trace an output entering the next stage. Ask whether the borrowing or speech stage exists and has run.
More calculation can recover discarded details
Ask students to distinguish two original records with the same retained value. No deterministic calculation of that value alone can know which original occurred.
A data type tells us what the data means
Compare a title, a summary and a full chapter. All can be text while supporting different questions.

blocks.text: INPUT  songs played, liked, or skipped
PROCESS  compare clues and rank possible songs
OUTPUT  a suggested song or a not-sure result
CORE IDEA  A system transforms information; it does not simply 'know.'

UNDER THE HOOD  Input, process, and output are functional roles. The process may contain human choices, fixed rules, calculations, retrieval, or a learned model. Naming the three stages prevents magical explanations of computer behavior.

blocks.caption: The first row is the kiosk as described. The later rows require additional components and actions. Arrows show information dependencies; they do not establish that every stage has actually run.

blocks.text: Notice the difference between a title, a description and an entire book. All three can be text, but they represent different amounts of information. Even a speech stage receiving three titles can speak only those supplied titles; it has not thereby read the full books. Always identify the content of an input, not just its data type.

A recommendation is also different from a loan. Selecting a title does not reserve a copy unless an authorised reservation step exists. Keeping these distinctions clear prevents us from crediting a system with actions it did not take.

blocks.text: CASE 1 — Camera app  Clue: photo enters before any result. Meaning: input.
CASE 2 — Music ranking  Clue: choices are compared and scored. Meaning: process.
CASE 3 — Song suggestion  Clue: a result is shown to the user. Meaning: output.
CASE 4 — No listening history  Clue: important input is missing. Meaning: not-sure case.
BOUNDARY  The output is not proof that the system understood the input as a person would.
